key_insight: GS-BMT establishes a large donor–recipient genomic research platform for transplantation, rather than an AI cancer drug discovery program.
clinical_relevance: The initiative aims to improve transplant risk prediction and donor selection, but the reported analyses do not establish clinical utility.
method: Profile 30,718 allogeneic transplant donor–recipient pairs using genome-wide genotyping, with sequencing and methylation profiling in selected subsets.
Compare Cox, random survival forest, and deep neural network models for survival prediction in 9,262 patients with AML.
Assess inherited CHIP susceptibility using polygenic scores in 19,750 donors.
evidence_signal: Clinical-variable survival models showed similarly modest discrimination (C-index: 0.63, 0.62, and 0.62), while donor CHIP polygenic scores were modestly lower in unrelated versus related donors.
watch_item: The illustrated doubling of donor risk relied on assumed polygenic-score effects, not demonstrated transplant outcomes.
paper_title: Genomic Studies in Blood and Marrow Transplantation (GS-BMT): An NCI-CIBMTR genomic medicine initiative in hematopoietic cell transplantation
